metadata.case_name: CHU TIK KWAN v. LIU TIK FOR T/A WING KWONG METAL SPRAYING WORKSHOP

plaintiff.occupation_before: worked at a factory making silk flowers operating a pressing machine

source: was splashed with burning thinners which in turn set fire to his clothing causing extensive burns over 40% of his body.
on 14th November, 1986 he had an operation to amputate his left little finger and to release the web space of the left thumb.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of other single finger

injuries.description: Stiff left ankle and left foot deformity due to contracture of scar tissue
source: The left ankle is stiff and the left foot deformed by contracture of scar tissue.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia or tendon at ankle or foot level

injuries.description: Left hand badly deformed with other fingers deformed and fused joints leading to lack of strength and dexterity
source: the left hand is badly deformed both by the little finger and adjacent part of the palm having been amputated, and the other fingers having deformed and fused joints with consequent lack of strength and dexterity.
injuries.icd_description: Combined traumatic amputation of finger with other parts of wrist or hand

injuries.description: Grossly disfiguring burn scars and surgical scars including large conspicuous surgical scar in left groin and pelvic region and surgical scar below right clavicle
injuries.body_part: lower half of trunk, both arms, both legs; left groin and pelvic region; below right clavicle
source: grossly disfiguring burn scats and scars from skin graft donor areas over much of the lower half of the front and back of his trunk, on both, his arms and. both legs In addition he has a large conspicuous surgical scat 32 cm by 8 mm crossed by 17 pairs of conspicuous stitch marks 30 mm in length in the left groin and pelvic region and a surgical scar 50 by 5 mm below the right clavicle.

injuries.description: Unstable skin grafts in lower one third of left leg prone to ulceration
injuries.body_part: lower one third of left leg
source: Dr. Nicholson is also of the opinion that the skin grafts particularly in the lower one third of his left leg are unstable and can be easily traumatised to cause ulceration and the Plaintiff has to take care to prevent trauma to this area.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

injuries.description: Noticeable muscle wasting in the leg
source: There is noticeable muscle wasting in the leg and he has difficulty in walking, and is unable to squat.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at lower leg level

manifestations.description: Severe pain at the time of the accident and extreme pain following many operations
Residual pain and discomfort, particularly pain in left foot when walking
Difficulty holding objects with left hand; lack of strength and dexterity
Ugly, appallingly disfiguring scars causing considerable distress
Frequently feels dizzy and short of breath
Unable to sweat from burnt and skin grafted areas; low tolerance to heat; requires air-conditioning for comfort
Bruises easily if bumps into anything
Ulcers in unstable skin of left leg

treatments_received: debridement and cleaning of burn wounds
operations to release contractures of the scar tissue
release of the web space of the left thumb
triple arthrodesis on the left ankle
visits by the community nursing service

losses.description: Grossly disfiguring burn scats and scars from skin graft donor areas over much of the lower half of the front and back of his trunk, on both his arms and both legs; large conspicuous surgical scat 32 cm by 8 mm crossed by 17 pairs of conspicuous stitch marks 30 mm in length in the left groin and pelvic region and a surgical scar 50 by 5 mm below the right clavicle.
Left hand badly deformed by amputation of the little finger and fused joints of other fingers with consequent lack of strength and dexterity.
Difficulty in walking, inability to squat, left ankle stiffness and left foot deformity from contracture of scar tissue.
Required assistance from his wife for feeding, going to the toilet, taking baths and other daily requirements of life during his recovery.
Unlikely, in view of his disabilities, to obtain remunerative employment again; plaintiff will not be able to work again.
